exposure.threats_to_validity: Exposure is a RANK among same-slot candidates, and the reference set was never length-matched. Two confounds, both real and both uncorrected. (1) SUM injects length directly into the rank on 6 of the 8 core slots — a longer candidate accrues more negative log-probability and ranks worse by length alone, up to a 1.75x length ratio within one slot; this is why the admissible reduction is the MEAN, against the research recommendation, since the statistic is used ordinally and never as an absolute log-probability. Neither is corrected because R cannot be length-matched without dropping |R| below the D-20 bit ceiling, and a smaller R costs more resolution than the confound costs accuracy. The per-slot token-length spread travels beside every exposure number so a reader sees which of the eight slots the confound can reach at all.
